quarantineRisk

An R package with an interactive Shiny app to explore how viral transmissibility (R0) and vaccine efficacy (VE) affect border quarantine breach risk.

Intended user: public health students and policy analysts.

Question the app helps answer: for a variant with a given R0, how much vaccine efficacy is needed to keep border-quarantine breach risk at or below an acceptable level, relative to the pre-Delta unvaccinated baseline?

Installation 

# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("ETC5523-2026/etc5523-assignment-4-yfan0161-stack")

Usage

Launch the interactive app 

library(quarantineRisk)
run_app()

Calculate risk for a single scenario 

calculate_risk(r0 = 6, ve = 0.6)      # risk relative to baseline
find_threshold_ve(r0 = 6, target = 1) # minimum VE to keep risk <= baseline

Data

The package includes quarantine_risk, a 100-row data frame (R0 = 1 to 10, VE = 0 to 0.9) giving total infection force relative to the pre-Delta unvaccinated baseline (1 = baseline). The values were transcribed from Figure 4 of Zachreson et al. (2022), COVID-19 in low-tolerance border quarantine systems: Impact of the Delta variant of SARS-CoV-2, Science Advances, 8(14), eabm3624 (https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.abm3624), which is open access under a CC BY 4.0 licence. The raw values and the preparation script are in data-raw/. Values are relative risks from simulation results, not probabilities of a breach.

AI-use declaration

Generative AI declaration: I used ChatGPT to suggest Shiny UI layout alternatives and help debug package build errors. I used Claude (Anthropic) to review my package against the assignment criteria and to suggest revisions to the Shiny app, the find_threshold_ve() function, tests, documentation and vignette. I checked, tested and revised all generated code and text.
